rows.speaker: أهل اللغة والمفسرون
rows.claim: Biyaʿ are churches of Christians.
rows.anchor: وهي كنيسة النصارى في قول أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق وأبو العباس
rows.claim: Ṣalawāt are Jewish synagogues; their Hebrew name is ṣalotā.
rows.anchor: هي كنائس اليهود، وهي بالعبرانية صلوتا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الضحاك، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Muqātil also identify ṣalawāt as synagogues.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك

words: وَمَسَاجِدُ يَذْكُرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: The mosques are those of the Muslim community of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني مساجد المسلمين من أمة محمد

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Without divine repelling, each prophetic dispensation's prayer places would have been demolished in its own era.
rows.anchor: لولا أن الله دفع بعض الناس ببعض لهدم في كل شريعة نبي

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: God's repelling people through others protects every community's worship places from corruption.
rows.anchor: أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه لولا دفعه الناس

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: The list is chronological: Israelite prayer places predated the Qurʾān, while mosques took their name later, so the oldest are named first.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بذكر البيع لأن صلوات من تقدم من أنبياء بني إسرائيل

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the view of most exegetes: God averts destruction of each religious community's worship places.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب أكثر أهل التأويل في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ṣalawāt means Muslim prayers, which cease if an enemy enters upon them.
rows.anchor: الصلوات: صلوات أهل الإسلام تنقطع إذا دخل عليهم العدو

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: On Ibn Zayd's reading, prayers are not demolished; an omitted phrase means that prayers are abandoned.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالصلوات لا تهدم، ولكن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: The intended referents are places where prayers are performed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: إنما يعني مواضع الصلوات

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first, era-by-era explanation is preferable.
rows.anchor: والقول هو الأول

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Believers protect the worship places of protected non-Muslims from demolition.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: يدفع عن هدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first view is preferable because the worship places were protected before their owners became dhimmīs; the alternative would list mosques first for their merit, while churches and synagogues were invalidated in Islam.
rows.anchor: لأنهم قبل أن صاروا أهل الذمة حين كانوا على الحق كانت متعبداتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God helps the one who supports His religion, law, and messenger.
rows.anchor: وهذا وعد من الله بنصر من ينصر دينه وشريعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The one supported is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ينصر محمدا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: God fulfilled the promise by helping Muhammad and his religious community.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: وقد فعل، نصر محمدا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Whoever establishes one of God's laws is helped to establish it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي: من أقام شريعة من شرائعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God is powerful over His creation and invincible in His dominion and power.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على خلقه {عزيز} منيع في سلطانه وقدرته

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: God is mighty in taking vengeance on His enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {عزيز} في انتقامه من عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every umma here is a generation that has passed.
rows.anchor: لكل قرن مضى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A manasak is a religious law practiced by that community.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد شريعة هم عاملون بها

rows.speaker: مقاتل وغيره
rows.claim: A manasak is an animal sacrifice offered at their festival.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل وغيره: يعني ذبيحة في عيدهم هم ذابحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manasak has already been discussed earlier in this sura.
rows.anchor: تقدم الكلام فيه في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter in which they must not dispute is animal sacrifice.
rows.anchor: يعني في أمر الذبائح

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: The verse concerned Badīl ibn Warqāʾ, Bishr ibn Sufyān, Yazīd ibn Khunays, and others who argued that animals killed by God were more deserving to eat than animals Muslims killed with knives.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: نزلت في بديل بن ورقاء الخزاعي

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The command means that the Prophet must not argue with them, as the following challenge shows.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى قوله {فلا ينازعنك} لا تنازعهم ولا تجادلهم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: This injunction came before fighting.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا قبل القتال

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Although they had argued, the reciprocal verb expresses a command not to argue with them; this construction works for mutual debate, unlike a one-way verb such as striking.
rows.anchor: لا يخاصمنك فلان في هذا أبدا، أي: لا تخاصمه

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling people to know Him through monotheism.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل بن سليمان: يعني إلى معرفة ربك وهو التوحيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The call is to uphold the ordinances of the pure monotheistic religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد قم بشرائع الحنيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken together, the command is to call to faith in God and practice the law He prescribed.
rows.anchor: والمعنى على هذا: ادع إلى الإيمان به وإعمال ما شرع من الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight guidance is the religion.
rows.anchor: قوله: {إنك لعلى هدى} دين {مستقيم} وهو قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: No religion created is more upright, excellent, or beloved to God than this one.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يخلق دينا أقوم ولا أفضل منه ولا أحب إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is Adam's descendant, since Adam himself was not a drop in a womb.
rows.anchor: يعني ابن آدم؛ لأن آدم لم يكن نطفة في رحم

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, the pronoun shifts to Adam's descendant rather than directly referring to the human named earlier; context licenses this inference.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول الأول عادت الكناية إلى ابن آدم لا إلى الإنسان المذكور في الآية الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contextual pronoun shift is compared with 5:101, where the pronoun refers to similar questions other than those just mentioned.
rows.anchor: لا تسألوا عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم وإن تسألوا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarār means a settled place or residence, named with a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: يعني مستقر، وموضع قرار، فسماه بالمصدر

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Makin means firmly settled, not unstable.
rows.anchor: قال المفضل: مطمئن غير مضطرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: The secure place is the womb, prepared to hold the embryo until its appointed term.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون في قوله: {مكين}: يريد الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages through the lump are explained earlier in the embryology passage in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.
rows.anchor: مفسر في سورة الحج إلى قوله: {فخلقنا المضغة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences are also read in the singular, ʿaẓman.
rows.anchor: وقرئ كلاهما (عظما) على الواحد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Singular and plural are valid: a person has many bones, a singular can imply a collection, and nearby flesh and the generic noun support that sense.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): التوحيد والجمع هاهنا جائزان

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The plural better matches Qurʾānic usage elsewhere; the singular is possible as a generic noun denoting a class or collection.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: الجمع أشبه بما جاء في التنزيل في غير هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، مجاهد، الشعبي، عكرمة، الربيع، أبو العالية، ابن زيد، القتيبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and the listed authorities interpret the new creation as breathing the spirit into the embryo; al-Qutaybī selects this view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني نفخ الروح فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the new creation is the growth of hair and teeth.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو نبات الشعر والأسنان

rows.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, and Mujāhid in some transmissions, interpret it as reaching full youth.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه قال: هو استواء الشباب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj offers another view: God made the embryo male or female.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزجاج قولا آخر وهو: أن جعل ذكرا وأنثى

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The spirit interpretation is strongest: changed wording marks a new beginning when formerly lifeless flesh and bone become a living creature.
rows.anchor: واختار صاحب النظم القول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the embryo's bones and flesh are fully formed, it is a human child, and a slave woman carrying it becomes an umm walad.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على أن الجنين إذا استوى عظمه ولحمه على العظم فقد صار إنسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves exaltation and praise, for He always has been and always will be.
rows.anchor: استحق التعظيم والثناء بأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn means the best image-makers or measurers.
rows.anchor: قوله: {أحسن الخالقين} أي: المصورين والمقدرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, khalq means measurement: leather is measured and fashioned to cut a flask, water skin, or shoe.
rows.anchor: العرب تقول: قدرت الأديم وخلقته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: People make things, but God makes too, and God is the best maker.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: وتصنعون ويصنع الله، والله خير الصانعين

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: A khāliq is a maker, and the feminine plural khāliqāt can refer to women makers.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: رجل خالق، أي: صانع. وهن الخالقات

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: God's making is better than sculptors' images, which do not move; yakhluqūn here means they make.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن سليمان: يقول: هو أحسن خلقا من الذين يخلقون التماثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafḥ means burning; fire or the hot sirocco is said to burn someone.
rows.anchor: معنى اللفح: الإحراق. يقال: لفحته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Talfaḥ and tanfaḥ have the same basic meaning, but talfaḥ has the stronger effect.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: تلفح وتنفح بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kulūḥ is exposing the teeth while scowling; related usage describes severe weather.
rows.anchor: الكلوح: بدو الأسنان (¬7) عند العبوس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: A kāliḥ has lips drawn back from the teeth, like a sheep's head with its teeth showing.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الكالح: الذي قد شمرت شفتاه عن أسنانه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd likens it to a head scorched by fire, its teeth showing and lips contracted.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود -في هذه الآية-: ألم تر إلى الرأس المشيط

rows.speaker: الخدري عن رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says the fire pulls the upper lip to the middle of the head and the lower lip to the navel.
rows.anchor: وروى الخدري، عن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: The signs in the next verse are the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
rows.claim: A woman from the Anṣār asked the Prophet what to do when male relatives entered while she was in a state in which she did not want to be seen; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: روى عدي بن ثابت (¬4) أن امرأة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: These are houses that do not belong to you.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني بيوتا ليست لكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، مقاتل، قتادة، السدي
rows.claim: Here tastaʾnisū means ask permission to enter.
rows.anchor: قال: يريد: حتى تستأذنوا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Istīdhān is seeking information; istinas means finding out whether residents want the visitor to enter.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى {تستأنسوا} في اللغة: تستأذنوا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Istīnas is learning who is in the house, as in saying one investigated and found nobody.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: الاستئناس: أن يعلم من في الدار

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: In Arabic, istīnas can mean looking to see who is in the house.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الاستئناس في كلام العرب: النظر

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse uses mustaʾnis for a wary creature scanning and turning to check for anything there.
rows.anchor: وقول النابغة: بذي الجليل (¬7) على مستأنس وحد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the wording should be until you ask permission, and calls tastaʾnisū a copyist's mistake.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {حتى تستأنسوا}

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
rows.claim: They explain istīnas as clearing the throat or sniffling to announce oneself, a kind of seeking information.
rows.anchor: وفسر مجاهد (¬1) والكلبي الاستئناس هنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين
rows.claim: They understand the wording by fronting and delaying: greet the residents, then request permission.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين. هذا على التقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh has the greeting-before-permission order, illustrated by comparable pairs in 3:43 and 64:2.
rows.anchor: وكذا هو في مصحف عبد الله مستقيم كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission is prescribed, entering another's house uninvited is forbidden, and the Sunnah greeting is السلام عليكم أأدخل.
rows.anchor: والسنة فيه أن يقول: السلام عليكم أأدخل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ask permission three times: the first lets the household hear, the second lets them prepare, and the third lets them admit or refuse; if refused, leave without lingering at their door.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة -في هذه الآية- كان يقال: الاستئذان ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: أبو موسى عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says permission is sought three times; if it is not granted, return.
rows.anchor: وقد روى أبو موسى، عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: This is purer for you and brings a greater reward.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أزكى لكم وأعظم لأجوركم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Asking permission is better than entering without it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أفضل لكم من أن تدخلوا بغير إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember that greeting and asking permission are good and follow them.
rows.anchor: أن السلام والاستئذان خير فتأخذون به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: It means so that you take admonition.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد كي تتعظوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They treat you only as someone to mock.
rows.anchor: أي: ما يتخذونك إلا مهزوؤا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mocking question means: Is this the man God sent to us as messenger?
rows.anchor: قالوا مستهزئين: أهذا الذي بعثه الله رسولا إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to idhā is an omitted qālū; the mockery clause interrupts between condition and response.
rows.anchor: وجواب {إذا} هو ما أضمر من القول

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The person recognizes God as deity and creator, yet desires and worships a stone; the verse asks his standing before God.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: أرأيت يا محمد من عرف

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Arabs sometimes worshipped whatever they desired, replacing a stone or tree with a better-looking one.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كانت العرب إذا هوى الرجل منهم شيئا عبده من دون الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic practice one might worship a stone, then replace it with a better one.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: كان أهل الجاهلية يعبد أحدهم الحجر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil identifies the example as al-Ḥārith ibn Qays al-Sahmī, who worshipped a stone he desired.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: وذلك أن الحارث بن قيس السهمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible parses supply an omitted preposition or make the god whatever he desires, naming the object by the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: تقدير الآية: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه بهواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line uses hawā for inclination or desire.
rows.anchor: هوى بتهامة وهوى بنجد ... فما أدري أنجد أم أغور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse expresses astonishment at their ignorance in worshipping what desire leads them to; desire leads to falsehood.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: تعجيب النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- من نهاية جهلهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ selects the interpretation that desire led them to worship an idol.
rows.anchor: باطل (¬7). وهذا القول اختيار الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view takes hawā as an idol worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الحسن وابن عباس؛ قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says such a person follows whatever he desires.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: لا يهوى شيئا إلا اتبعه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the second view as obeying and following desire without regard for consequences.
rows.anchor: فقال في القول الثاني: أي: أطاع هواه، وركبه فلم يبال عاقبة ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the person follows desire, abandons truth, and treats desire like a god.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار ابن قتيبة؛ قال: يقول: يتبع هواه ويدع الحق فهو كالإله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet is not a controller over him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لست عليه بمسيطر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The Prophet does not control the person's choice to follow desire and error.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يريد أن تكون بيدك المشيئة في الهوى والضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot guard someone from following desire and worshipping what he desires instead of God.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أفأنت عليه حافظ، تحفظه من اتباع هواه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse was abrogated by the fighting verse.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: نسختها آية القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those asked to look are the people who deny the message.
rows.anchor: يعني هؤلاء المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vegetation grows after the earth had been dead and without plants.
rows.anchor: بعد أن كانت ميتة لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: This means every kind of fruit and other fine, pleasant thing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: من كل صنف من أصناف الفواكه وغير ذلك حسن طيب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Karīm means beautiful in appearance.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: من كل ضرب حسن في المنظر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The phrase refers to plants eaten by people and livestock.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is compared with the matching expression in 22:5 and 50:7.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {من كل زوج بهيج}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Idh is accusative with an implied command to recount this story; the following command to recount Abraham's story supplies evidence.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: موضع {إذ} نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is to address someone with yā so-and-so; God called Moses after he saw the tree and fire.
rows.anchor: ومعنى النداء: الدعاء ب: يا فلان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال ابن # عباس: يريد: المشركين

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They wronged themselves through disbelief and sin, and wronged Israelites by imposing grievous torment.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: يعني الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بالكفر والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage next identifies them as Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثم أخبر عنهم فقال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says tattaqūn is valid because Moses was to address them; yat-taqūn is also valid because the revelation begins before direct address, as in 3:12.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لو قرئ: {ألا تتقون} بالتاء

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Stop after qawmu Firʿawn because its meaning is complete; the following words begin a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: قوله {قوم فرعون} وقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks why they do not avert God's punishment by obeying Him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: {ألا يتقون} ألا يصرفون عن أنفسهم عقوبة الله بطاعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: The act was Moses' killing of the Copt.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: يعني قتل القبطي الذي قتله موسى

rows.speaker: الحسن والسدي
rows.claim: One reading is that Moses disbelieved in Pharaoh's god and followed the religion he now criticizes.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد، مقاتل، عطاء، العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another reading is ingratitude for Pharaoh's favors: he raised Moses and treated him well, yet Moses killed one of his people.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن زيد ومقاتل وعطاء

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh did not understand disbelief in the Lord as the charge here.
rows.anchor: والعوفي، عن ابن عباس قال: إن فرعون لم يكن يعلم ما الكفر بالربوبية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ selects ingratitude for Pharaoh's favor of raising Moses.
rows.anchor: واختاره الفراء فقال (¬3): وأنت الآن من الكافرين

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Pharaoh's reply belittles the caller to God out of arrogance, redirecting the discussion from its proper subject.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: هذا الجواب من فرعون لموسى استصغار لحال الداعي

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The feminine verb is used with masculine qawm because the intended sense is the group, jamāʿat qawm Nūḥ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: دخلت التاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والمفسرون
rows.claim: The plural messengers refers specifically to Noah; rejecting one messenger is rejecting them all, since each commands belief in all messengers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومقاتل، والمفسرون: يعني نوحا وحده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the last messenger brings what the first brought, so rejecting one is rejecting them all.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الحسن؛ لما سئل عن هذا وأمثاله فقال

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī means Noah and what he told them about later messengers.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي {كذبت قوم نوح} نوحا، وما أخبرهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows that they rejected all messengers.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وجائز أن يكونوا كذبوا جميع الرسل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين
rows.claim: Noah was their brother by lineage, not religion; he was one of their own people.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ابن أبيهم، يعني: أن الأخوة كانت من جهة النسب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Every messenger comes speaking his people's language to make the proof clearer to them.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: كل رسول يأتي بلسان قومه، ليوضح لهم الحجة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation cites 14:4 to support that every messenger speaks his people's language so the proof is clearer.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression was explained earlier in this sura, asking why people do not avert God's punishment by obedience.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ألا تتقون} مفسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: God entrusted Noah with the message and sent him to his people; he is trustworthy in conveying it between them and their Lord.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ائتمني الله على رسالته، وبعثني إليكم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Noah had already been trustworthy among his people.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان فيهم أمينا قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear God by obeying and worshipping Him.
rows.anchor: {فاتقوا الله} بطاعته وعبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obey Noah in his command to believe and affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: {وأطيعون} فيما آمركم به من الإيمان والتوحيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Noah warns them of the Fire and clarifies what brings them nearer to God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنذركم النار، وأبين لكم ما يقربكم من الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Noah says he is only a clear messenger.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ما أنا إلا رسول بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means: if Noah does not stop speaking and keep quiet.
rows.anchor: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا نوح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-marjūmīn means those who are killed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومقاتل، والكلبي: من المقتولين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets it as those insulted or reviled.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: من المشتومين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets it as those pelted with stones.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: المضروبين بالحجارة

words: مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God created for them from their spouses refers to their wives' sexual organs.
rows.anchor: ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم} يعني: فروج نسائهم

words: مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid paraphrases their conduct as abandoning women's front openings for men's rear openings.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تركتم أقبال النساء إلى أدبار الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are unjust transgressors who cross from the lawful to the unlawful and obedience to sin.
rows.anchor: بل أنتم قوم عادون} ظالمون معتدون الحلال إلى الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here it means if Lot does not stop speaking.
rows.anchor: لئن لم تنته} لئن لم تسكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They threaten to expel Lot from their town and village.
rows.anchor: لتكونن من المخرجين} من بلدتنا وقريتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat parallels what the people told Shuʿayb in 7:88.
rows.anchor: كقولهم لشعيب: {لنخرجنك يا شعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Those who disobey the Prophet are his close relatives.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد عشيرتك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil specifies Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني بني هاشم وبني المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet disavows their disbelief and worship of other than God.
rows.anchor: أي: من الكفر وعبادة غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that alliance with a polytheist is forbidden in every case, since God commands this even for the Prophet's closest relatives.
rows.anchor: والآية دليل على أن موالاة المشرك حرام بكل حال

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Entrust all your affairs to God.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: فوض إليه جميع أمرك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Trust God, who is mighty in punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ثق بالله {العزيز} في نقمته

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: God is merciful to them by not hastening their punishment.
rows.anchor: {الرحيم} بهم حين لم يعجل عليهم بالعقوبة
